strengths: Clear practical motivation and substantial demonstrated impact: 4× inference speedup on long sequences, 34% training cost reduction, and enabling new applications (e.g., 30% longer sequences in BoltzDesign)
Comprehensive experimental evaluation across multiple model sizes, benchmarks (RCSB, CASP15), and strong baselines (AlphaFold3, Chai-1, Boltz-1) with detailed FLOPs calculations

Insightful analysis revealing the role of pair representations (93.7% win rate on distance metrics) and sparsity in triangle multiplication (low-norm dropout analysis showing robustness when 75% of features are zeroed)
Excellent reproducibility with extensive hyperparameters, detailed FLOPs breakdowns, algorithmic specifications, and implementation details
Rigorous ablation studies on FFN dimensions, triangle multiplication dimensions, alternative mixing methods, and down-stream applications (BindFast)
weaknesses: Limited conceptual novelty: primarily an architectural simplification/ablation study (removing triangle attention) rather than a fundamental advance. Triangle multiplication was already known and used in AlphaFold

Marginal and inconsistent performance gains: on RCSB large model Pairmixer matches Pairformer (0.78 lDDT), but lags on DockQ>0.23 (0.63 vs 0.64) and shows mixed results on CASP15. Performance is comparable rather than improved

Insufficient mechanistic analysis of why this works: the paper shows triangle multiplication is sufficient but doesn't deeply explain *why* or why removing sequence attention causes minimal performance loss. Section 6 analysis is somewhat observational

Design choice justifications lack empirical validation: the claim that removing sequence updates is justified because MSA information now flows through pair representation is not systematically tested. Why not keep sequence updates with triangle multiplication?

Experimental design ambiguities: oracle vs top-1 evaluation can mask degradation; Pairmixer lacks trained confidence model while baselines have one; matching training duration rather than FLOPs makes smaller model comparisons non-equivalent; no formal statistical significance testing despite overlapping error bars
Limited scope of downstream applications: only BindFast thoroughly evaluated for downstream tasks. Virtual screening, proteome-wide folding, and other applications lack concrete benchmarking
Missing comparisons with related simplification methods (MiniFold, SimpleFold) that were mentioned but not directly compared
Primarily empirical contribution with limited theoretical insights into why pair representations and triangle operations are fundamental to structure prediction

strengths: Well-motivated problem addressing a genuine computational bottleneck in structure prediction at scale with concrete practical examples
Counter-intuitive and elegant core finding that triangle attention can be removed without performance degradation, demonstrated convincingly across multiple model sizes and benchmarks
Comprehensive experimental evaluation with multiple datasets (RCSB, CASP15), baselines (AlphaFold3, Chai-1, Boltz-1), metrics (lDDT, DockQ, lDDT-PLI, RMSD), and oracle/top-1 evaluations
Strong practical impact with substantial efficiency gains (4× inference speedup on long sequences, 34% training cost reduction, 2-2.6× binder design speedup, 30% longer sequences enabled)

Insightful analysis including head-to-head comparisons (93.7% win rate on lDDT), sparsity analysis via dropout experiments showing triangle multiplication captures essential sparse interactions, and Match3 task analysis isolating representation effects
High reproducibility with detailed hyperparameters, complete FLOPs breakdown, algorithmic specifications, and multiple trained model sizes from scratch
Thorough ablations varying FFN hidden dimension, triangle multiplication dimension, alternative mixing methods, and diffusion depth, systematically analyzing design choices
Clear presentation with well-designed figures and tables; practical demonstration of downstream application value (BindFast)
weaknesses: Limited architectural novelty—core contribution is removing components from Pairformer rather than introducing new concepts; primarily an engineering contribution rather than methodological advance

Incomplete mechanistic understanding of why triangle attention is redundant; sparsity analysis is suggestive but indirect, and doesn't fully explain how triangle multiplication captures triangle attention's role

Noticeable performance gaps on key metrics: DockQ >0.23 shows 0.63 vs. 0.64 (Boltz-1) on RCSB and 0.62 vs. 0.68 on CASP15; these differences receive limited discussion and no systematic analysis of failure modes
Missing confidence model (results marked with *) affects practical comparisons and deployment relevance; no discussion of when this will be addressed

Sequence update removal justified only indirectly; lacks direct ablation demonstrating sequence updates are unnecessary, and efficiency argument is weaker (quadratic vs. cubic cost) than for triangle attention removal

Transformer baseline receives substantial architectural modifications (s_msa extraction, z_backbone from outer sum) beyond simple sequence-only design, making it unclear whether advantage comes from pair representations or Pairmixer-specific choices
No systematic error analysis or characterization of when Pairmixer underperforms; practitioners lack guidance on structure types or interaction modes where Pairformer might be preferable

Downstream application evaluation limited primarily to runtime metrics; design quality comparison in BindFast only qualitative (Figure 13); scope limited to binder design despite claims about broader applications

Title 'Triangle Multiplication is All You Need' is misleading (FFN is also essential); critical design choice justifications relegated to appendix; statistical significance of performance differences not discussed given sample sizes
Match3 task analysis, while illustrative, is somewhat artificial and may not capture structure prediction complexity; limited connection to main narrative

strengths: Comprehensive experimental evaluation across diverse benchmarks (RCSB, CASP15, multiple biomolecular interaction types) with rigorous comparisons to state-of-the-art (AF3, Chai-1, Boltz-1)

Clear practical impact addressing real computational bottlenecks: 4× inference speedup on long sequences, 34% training cost reduction, enables applications like BindFast for larger protein design targets

Thorough analysis of design choices: pair representation ablation showing 93.7% win rate on pairwise metrics, sparsity analysis via low-norm vs random dropout, distogram evaluation isolating backbone contribution
Strong empirical validation maintaining comparable accuracy while improving efficiency: mean LDDT of 0.78 at large scale matching Pairformer with only 66% training time
Excellent reproducibility: code availability, comprehensive hyperparameter details (Table 10), multiple model sizes tested, stratified performance analysis by sequence length and MSA depth
weaknesses: Limited architectural novelty: core contribution is removing triangle attention and sequence updates from Pairformer—primarily an ablation study rather than fundamental innovation. Title 'Triangle Multiplication is All You Need' overstates contribution (still relies on triangle multiplication + FFN + diffusion module)

Insufficient justification for key design choices: claim that sequence updates are unnecessary because MSA Module now encodes evolutionary information lacks rigor for AlphaFold3-style models; ablations (Table 6) only at small scale (12 layers, 3M samples) versus full model (48 layers, 6.8M+ samples)

Performance gaps across metrics not fully addressed: RCSB DockQ > 0.23 (0.63 vs 0.64), CASP15 gaps including medium-scale DockQ > 0.23 (0.50 vs 0.68); RNA structures where Transformer slightly outperforms; suggests simplification loses discriminative capacity

Sparsity analysis insufficient to justify triangle multiplication replaces triangle attention: low-norm dropout stability doesn't prove design learns sparse features by necessity; block-dropout degradation at B=512 could indicate global dependencies rather than sparse long-range interactions

Ablation quality concerns: main ablations at small scale with limited training; statement 'Pairmixer recovers performance with additional training' lacks full-scale evidence; transformer baseline required special engineering (outer sum construction) suggesting unfair comparison

Limited downstream application rigor: BindFast evaluation focuses on speedup not accuracy; Figure 13 'comparable designs' lacks quantitative metrics; no systematic analysis of problem classes where Pairmixer underperforms

Modest efficiency gains at practical scales: 4× speedup only achieved at extreme sequence lengths (2048 tokens); default setting shows only 1.6× speedup (21 vs 34 seconds); speedup diminishes with more recycling

Missing failure mode analysis: no discussion of systematic underperformance; limited explanation of why triangle multiplication captures triangle attention's capabilities; no comparison to related simplification work (MiniFold)
